summary: Intermittent SMB/NetBIOS name resolution and file-share resets over WireGuard after network handoffs (MTU/fragmentation suspected)
description:
Issue summary:
Users on corporate laptops intermittently lose access to SMB file shares and cannot resolve NetBIOS/hostname for internal file servers when connected over WireGuard VPN, typically after switching between Wi‑Fi and a docked Ethernet adapter.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers on us-west experiencing file-share failures and long delays opening network folders.
- Affected workflows: git-lfs pulls to SMB-backed stores and shared build artifacts.
- No total outage, but productivity impact reported across 5-10 users this week.

Environment:
- Client OS: Windows 11 (22000+ builds) and a few Windows 10 devices.
- VPN: WireGuard-based company VPN (user-space daemon via corporate agent).
- Network: Office Wi‑Fi (802.11ax) and USB-C dock to wired Ethernet.
- Internal servers: smb01.corp.redwood (10.24.5.12), smb02.corp.redwood (10.24.5.13).

Observed start time: 2026-03-09 08:30 PDT (first report), recurring through 2026-03-11.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Connect laptop to corporate Wi‑Fi and establish WireGuard VPN.
2) Mount \\smb01.corp.redwood\shared from Explorer or net use.
3) Walk the client to a dock and plug into Ethernet (or attach dock while machine awake) so Windows switches default route/interface.
4) Attempt to access previously-opened network paths or resolve smb01.corp.redwood via ping/nbtstat.
5) Observe intermittent ping failures, long SMB open times, and occasional immediate session resets.

Note: problem is intermittent; reproduces more reliably if applications keep sockets open during the handoff (e.g., Explorer window with network folder open).
observed_behavior:
- DNS A lookups succeed to internal IPs but NetBIOS name resolution (nbtstat) times out intermittently.
- SMB sessions show STATUS_NETWORK_NAME_DELETED / STATUS_CONNECTION_RESET in client event logs.
- Packet captures show fragmented TCP segments that are not reassembled by the server-side firewall; subsequent retransmits lead to long stalls then session reset.
- Some clients work if the VPN is reconnected after the interface change; others require a reboot of the networking stack.
expected_behavior:
- Seamless interface handoff with persistent WireGuard session and continued SMB/NetBIOS name resolution.
- No dropped SMB sessions purely due to MTU/interface changes during an active connection.
logs:
Client-side Windows Event Log extracts (anonymized):
- EventID 4227: TCP connection lost to 10.24.5.12:445 after network change.
- SMBClient: STATUS_CONNECTION_RESET repeated during file copy.
- WireGuard logs: persistent tunnel, but peer endpoint path changes from Wi‑Fi IP to Ethernet IP after handoff.

Server-side firewall logs:
- Dropped fragments: fragment offset non-zero but 'DF' bit handling show larger than allowed MTU on firewall path; firewall logs show 'fragmented packet dropped - reassembly table full' around incidents.

Attached pcap samples taken on client during reproduction window (reference IDs): pcap-client-0309-0832.pcap (stored on internal diagnostics S3).
packet_capture_summary:
- Observed large SMB packets (window scaling) crossing tunnel with MSS 1420 on client side but path MTU reduced to ~1350 on intermediate device after handoff.
- Fragmented TCP payloads with subsequent retransmissions. Server side or intermediate firewall drops some fragments (likely due to reassembly table limits or DF mismatch).
- When client renegotiates MSS (after re-establishing tunnel) behavior normalizes.
- Evidence points to an interaction between interface handoff, WireGuard path MTU discovery, and a middlebox that drops fragments during reassembly windows.
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced on two independent devices in lab with controlled Wi‑Fi -> Ethernet transition.
- Brought up temporary bypass: disabling 'EnablePMTU' on WireGuard client causes smaller segments and stabilizes SMB sessions (mitigation only).
- Middlebox team (edge firewall) confirms older appliance in branch office has small IP reassembly buffer and aggressive fragment-dropping when multiple rapid path changes occur.
- Ticket INT-424246 (linked) shows previous related MTU/blackhole symptoms for other VPN flows; similar fingerprint but different protocol (gRPC vs SMB).
- Hypothesis: Windows preserves large TCP windows across interface change; WireGuard doesn't immediately renegotiate MSS, so a burst of large packets is emitted and some fragments are dropped until PMTU/DPLP handshake completes.

Temporary test action: forced MSS clamping on WireGuard shim on pilot group (MSS=1200) and users report stable file-share access during handoffs.
comments: Priya Desai (Reporter) 2026-03-11: Noticed multiple reports this morning after return from meeting — users had Explorer windows open and then plugged into dock. All reported slow file list load or 'network path not found'.

Evan Brooks (Assignee) 2026-03-11: Confirmed I can reproduce in lab. Captured pcap from client during handoff. Suspect PMTU/path reassembly interaction. Escalating to edge-firewall team for middlebox behavior review.

Jordan Kim (Edge FW) 2026-03-11: Edge team: We're running older Reassemble-Engine v2.1 on some branch edge devices; default reassembly table is small for high concurrency. Can temporarily increase table and enable fragment-tolerant mode. Will schedule change in next maintenance window if approved.

Marta Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-12: Applied temporary MSS clamp on pilot configuration for corporate agent (MSS=1200). Pilot users (5 devices) reported no further drops on repeated tests. Need to evaluate perf impact and rollout plan.
Evan Brooks 2026-03-12: Filed infra PR to add MSS clamp flag to WireGuard client profile and created follow-up task to coordinate firewall reconfig with Edge team.
actions_taken:
- Reproduced locally and captured pcaps.
- Coordinated with Edge FW team; they proposed reassembly-table increase.
- Deployed temporary client-side MSS clamp (MSS=1200) to 5 pilot users via corp agent; all pilot users successful.
- Opened infra PR github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1728 to support MSS clamp flag in client profiles.
- Notified support channel #internal-netops and #edge-firewall.
next_steps:
- Schedule firewall reassembly table increase and fragment-tolerant mode on affected edge appliances (maintenance window required).
- If firewall change not possible soon, roll out MSS clamp flag to broader user cohort with monitoring.
- Update VPN client runbook with recommended setting for Windows handoffs.
- Post-change: run 48h smoke tests for SMB flows and gather metric on SMB session resets.
- Close ticket once changes are validated and follow-up PR merged.
resolution:
Workaround deployed: MSS clamp (1200) pushed to pilot group which eliminated reproductions. Edge FW team to increase reassembly capacity in next maintenance window. Permanent mitigation will be a combination of middlebox configuration and optional client MSS clamp.

Resolution notes: Coordinate change window with Edge FW and Infra teams; update runbook and roll out MSS clamp via corp agent if appliance upgrade is delayed.
